remarks: No tracked port is under a weather or closure entry this run, and that is the correct state rather than a gap. Typhoon Saudel and Tropical Storm Krovanh are long gone, the Shanghai/Ningbo entry aged out of its two-day window on 14 September as designed, and nothing since has justified reopening it. Shanghai/Ningbo is still carrying a heavy queue — 1.34M TEU at anchorage and a queue-to-berth ratio of 2.14 on the 13 September snapshot — but that is post-typhoon bunching plus the pre-Golden Week rush, not an active weather event, so the congestion data should speak for itself and the site's own idle-berth flag is deliberately left unsuppressed.

TC2630 is the only active system and it is not a supply-chain event. It has drifted about 230 km closer to the tracked ports since the 14 September read (closest approach to Busan tightened from 1,188 km to 959 km) but the forecast track still runs north and north-northwest through open ocean east of Japan, never inside the 600 km radius of any tracked port. It does reach typhoon strength around +69h, so it is worth re-reading next run rather than dismissing.

Last week's only operational closures were outside the tracked set: Dalian lost 32 hours and Lianyungang 14.5 hours to gale-force Bohai winds, both since resumed. Qingdao, the nearest tracked port to that weather, stayed open and fluid at 76% yard occupancy.
The Kuehne+Nagel weekly waiting-time table for 9-15 September has not been published yet, so no reported berth waiting figures were available to attach to any port. None were estimated.
